skill.name: iterate-pr
skill.description: Guides an agent through checking a pull request, reading CI and review feedback, making targeted fixes, and waiting for passing checks.
skill.summary: Guides iterative PR fixes until CI and review feedback are resolved.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: I found no prompt-injection text, obfuscation, credential theft, or hidden network endpoint in SKILL.md. Most static alerts are Markdown command examples, inline labels, or source metadata rather than executable scripts. I confirmed the commit-and-push step as a medium risk because it can stage all local changes and mutate the remote branch.

remediation.issue: Broad staging before push can include unrelated local changes.
remediation.suggestion: Tell the agent to show status and diff, stage only intended files, and ask before pushing.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use current branch substitution without quoting.
remediation.suggestion: Capture the branch name in a variable and quote it in GitHub CLI and git push commands.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on authenticated GitHub and git commands.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands should run only in the intended repository and branch with user authorization.

static_findings.snippet: The `bucket` field categorizes state into: `pass`, `fail`, `pending`, `skipping`, or `cancel`.
**Important:** If any of these checks are still `pending`, wait before proceeding:
- All CI checks are green (`bucket: pass`)
- Use `gh pr checks --required` to focus only on required checks
- Use `gh run view <run-id> --verbose` to see all job steps, not just failures
4. **Skip invalid feedback** - If the concern is not legitimate, move on

content.user_title: Iterate Pull Requests Until CI Passes
content.value_statement: CI failures and review comments can slow pull request delivery. This skill guides an agent through checking status, fixing issues, pushing updates, and waiting for green checks.
actual_capabilities: Finds the pull request for the current branch with GitHub CLI.
Checks PR status, review decisions, comments, and CI buckets.
Retrieves inline review comments and PR conversation comments.
Reads failed GitHub Actions logs before deciding what to fix.
Guides minimal code edits, commits, pushes, and CI waiting.
Stops when failures persist, feedback needs clarification, or no PR exists.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI session and repository access.
Assumes the agent may edit files, create commits, and push to the branch.
Does not guarantee that every CI failure is caused by branch changes.
May need user decisions for unclear feedback or repeated failures.

use_cases.title: Fix a PR With Failing CI
use_cases.description: Diagnose failed checks, read logs, make targeted fixes, and wait for a clean run.

use_cases.title: Close Review Feedback Quickly
use_cases.description: Collect human and bot comments, verify each issue, and apply only valid changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Branch for Merge
use_cases.description: Repeat the check, fix, push, and wait loop until quality gates are satisfied.

prompt_templates.title: Check My PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a first CI status pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the iterate-pr skill on the current branch. Find the PR, check CI status, and tell me what needs attention before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Clear CI Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the iterate-pr skill to inspect failed checks, read the relevant logs, make minimal fixes, and show me the planned commit before pushing.

prompt_templates.title: Address Review Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for human and bot comments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the iterate-pr skill to gather review comments and bot feedback. Verify each item, fix valid issues, and skip feedback that is already resolved.

prompt_templates.title: Run the Full Iteration Loop
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with guardrails for repeated attempts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the iterate-pr skill to repeat status checks, fixes, commits, pushes, and CI waits. Stop after three similar failures or when you need my decision.

output_examples.input: The PR has one failed test job and one pending code coverage check.
output_examples.output: The agent reports the pending check, reads the failed job logs, proposes a focused test fix, and waits before handling coverage feedback.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks for a naming change and a bot reports a lint failure.
output_examples.output: The agent verifies both comments, changes the valid naming issue, fixes the lint failure, and summarizes the branch update.

output_examples.input: The same integration test fails after three attempts.
output_examples.output: The agent stops the loop, explains the repeated failure pattern, and asks for user guidance before continuing.

best_practices: Review status and diff before allowing commits or pushes.
Let bot checks finish before fixing related feedback.
Stop after repeated failures and ask the user for context.
anti_patterns: Do not push unrelated local changes while fixing a PR.
Do not assume a failed check name explains the root cause.
Do not loop indefinitely when CI keeps failing.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow expects an authenticated GitHub CLI session in the target repository.

faq.question: Can it push commits to my branch?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow includes committing fixes and pushing to the current branch.

faq.question: Does it read review comments?
faq.answer: Yes. It gathers review status, inline comments, PR conversation comments, and bot feedback.

faq.question: Does it decide every review comment is valid?
faq.answer: No. The workflow says to verify feedback and skip items that are invalid or already fixed.

faq.question: When should the agent stop?
faq.answer: It should stop when no PR exists, a rebase is needed, failures repeat, or user clarification is required.

faq.question: Is it limited to GitHub pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The process is built around GitHub CLI, GitHub Actions checks, and GitHub PR comments.
